cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ, is writing to the church in Corinth, and back in chapter 10 he's been defending his work against some rivals who commend themselves. Now he asks the Corinthians for a little patience: “I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.” HA, that's me asking a baker to sit through one more junk drawer story, and the baker going, PAPA, I've been sitting through them since hello!
Then Paul says he's jealous for them, and he's quick to add it's a godly jealousy. He paints a wedding picture: he promised them to one husband, and he wants to present them pure.

cards.question: In Paul's wedding picture, he promised the Corinthians to one husband. Who is the husband?

cards.text: But Paul is worried. He reaches all the way back to the garden in Genesis, to someone who got deceived by the serpent.

cards.question: Paul writes to the Corinthians that ___ was deceived by the serpent's cunning.
Just like Eve, Paul is afraid the Corinthians' minds could be led astray from their simple and pure devotion to Christ.

cards.text: Paul spells out the danger: someone preaching a Jesus other than the One Paul preached, a different spirit, a different gospel. Friend, that's not a new flavor, that's a whole different cookie wearing the old label!

cards.question: If someone comes preaching a different Jesus or a different gospel, how does Paul say the Corinthians handle it?

answers.text: They put up with it very easily
They send the preacher away fast
They argue about it for days

cards.text: Then Paul brings up a group he calls those “super-apostles.” I don't know about you, friend, but I'm picturing CAPES.

cards.question: How does Paul say he measures up next to those super-apostles?

cards.text: Paul admits he's not a polished speaker. Hey, ME NEITHER, friend, my greatest speech ever was to a scared can opener in the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: Paul says that besides not being a polished speaker, he's lacking in knowledge too.

cards.text: Then Paul asks the Corinthians a question with a little edge on it. Was it a sin for him to humble himself so he could lift them up?

cards.question: What did Paul do in Corinth that he's asking the Corinthians about?

answers.text: Preached the gospel free of charge
Refused to stay in anyone's home

cards.text: Paul says he “robbed other churches” by accepting their support so he could serve the Corinthians. ROBBED, friend, the most polite heist in history!

cards.question: When Paul was in Corinth and in need, the brothers who came from ___ supplied his needs.
Paul hasn't been a burden to the Corinthians in any way. What's his plan from here?

answers.text: Never be a burden to them

cards.text: Paul says nobody in the regions of Achaia is going to silence his boasting about serving the Corinthians free, “As surely as the truth of Christ is in me.” Then he asks why he won't take their support, and friend, you can hear the hurt in it: “Why? Because I do not love you?”

cards.question: Paul answers his own question by saying God knows he loves the Corinthians.

cards.text: So Paul isn't changing a thing. He's going to keep on doing what he's doing, like me and the snooze button, friend, except his reason is WAY better.

cards.question: Why will Paul keep preaching to the Corinthians free of charge?

answers.text: To undercut men who want to seem his equals
To save up for a trip out to Spain
To set an example for the Macedonians

cards.question: Paul calls the men who want to be seen as his equals ___ apostles and deceitful workers.

cards.text: Paul says these men are masquerading as apostles of Christ. And no wonder, he says, because someone else wears a disguise like that too.

cards.question: Who does Paul say masquerades as an angel of light?

cards.text: So Paul says it's not surprising if Satan's servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Friend, I met a REAL angel once, in a junk drawer in the dark, and let me tell you, the real thing never needs a costume.

cards.question: Paul says these false apostles will get away with what they're doing in the end.
